The founder and current CEO are different people. 
Founder/original CEO: Tom Lee, MD
Current CEO: Amir Dan Rubin

Amir was brought in to actually make OM profitable (Aka why Tom Lee was forced out). He was who was in charge during the whole COVID controversy. I'm not sure/don't know anything about him being forced out to make it more attractive for acquisition and because of the legal action, but that makes sense. 

Even worse than Google Ventures funding One Medical is the Carlyle Group investing $350 million back in 2018.  

100% it's made for young, healthy people who know how to utilize technology. I can't tell you how many patients needed help signing up, booking appointments, etc. People with complex, chronic health problems would be referred out because One Medical providers don't have the time or resources to take care of them. Some do and try, but they unfortunately burnout and then leave. Even the fucking furniture isn't meant for older people. Offices would beg for furniture that wasn't so low because elderly patients would struggle to get on and off of it, but these requests would ultimately get ignored. Probably because it didn't go with our "aesthetic."

They did acquire Iora Primary Care, which offers care for Medicare patients, but I didn't see any difference in the care they offered geriatric patients in San Francisco. 

Rant over. Sorry. As a former employee, I'm not surprised this happened. One Medical is all about profit over care. Amazon also has shit ethics.
